received a conditional or unconditional offer of study at lse. - sucessfully submitted a graduate financial support application. it is recommend that your application for admission is submitted well in advance of the deadline. read the guidance on when to apply for admission . notification of decisions after submitting your graduate financial support application, please allow up to 24 hours to receive a decision on your eligibility for the graduate support scheme. the decision will be made available on the graduate application portal. the information you provide on your graduate financial support application will also be used to consider you for any other scholarships we have available for which you meet the eligibility criteria. we will only contact successful applicants regarding the outcome of these awards. successful applicants will be notified throughout may, june and july. please ensure 'lse.ac.uk' is added to your email account 'safe senders' list to avoid any email notification going to your junk inbox. if you do not receive a response by the end of july, your scholarship application has not been successful. due to the number of applications received each year, we are not able to provide individual feedback about your application. share fees and funding scholarships, studentships, loans and tuition fees how to apply the application process, ucas and when to apply undergraduate fees and funding details on available scholarships, bursaries, loans and tuition fees graduate fees and funding details on available scholarships, bursaries, loans and tuition fees contact us get in touch with the financial support office meet, visit and discover lse webinars, videos, on campus events and visits around the world

years. esrc studentships cover full fees (for overseas students, lse will cover the difference between uk and overseas fees) and an annual stipend of £23805. there is additional dtp funding available study abroad summer school global and online degrees international students meet, visit and discover lse close search go lse csc scholarship lse is proud to partner with the china scholarship council (csc) to offer the lse-csc scholarship. this prestigious scholarship supports outstanding students from china in pursuing their research degree at lse. funding details lse is pleased to offer up to eight scholarships each academic year. these scholarships are tenable for up to four years and recipients must be enrolled in a full time study mode. the lse-csc scholarship covers: full tuition fees an annual stipend of £1350 per month overseas health insurance a round-trip economy class airfare between china and the uk reimbursement of a one-time visa application fee eligibility candidates must be citizens of the people's republic of china. overseas chinese students may be eligible for application subject to csc policy at the time. more information can be found here: https://www.csc.edu.cn/ . candidates must hold an unconditional offer of admission to an mphil/phd programme. candidates should satisfy other application criteria set out by csc. more information can be found here: https://www.csc.edu.cn/ . successful candidates agree to return to china upon completion of your research degree at lse. how to apply there is no separate application for any of these studentships. you will be considered automatically based on your application for admission. step one: candidates need to have submitted a complete application for admission to the graduate admissions office before the application deadline of wednesday 14 january 2026 23:59 uk time. some departments will have an earlier deadline. refer to the individual programme page for the relevant deadline information find your graduate programme . step two: by friday 20 march 2026 , the financial support office will notify nominated candidates of their nomination for the lse-csc scholarship to the china scholarship council for their decision. step three: nominated candidates must submit a separate application to the csc. application guidance is on the csc official website: http://www.csc.edu.cn the csc application deadline is 01 april 2026 14:00 beijing time . step four: csc will evaluate the nominated candidates according to csc requirements and inform successful candidates via the csc website. step five: lse will contact successful candidates separately in early july 2026 to confirm the decision. contact: for any questions relating to this lse-csc scholarship, please email pages.https://www.leeds.ac.uk/scholarship/9/le: skip to main content university of leeds homepage search leeds.ac.uk search all leeds.ac.uk leeds alumni discount if you are a graduate of the university of leeds and are considering further study, you may be eligible for a 10% tuition fee discount. value 10% tuition fee discount fee status uk, international study level postgraduate final deadline ongoing contact details email the admissions enquiries team at study@leeds.ac.uk eligibility to be eligible you must: have studied an undergraduate or postgraduate degree at the university of leeds, the swjtu-leeds joint school or an affiliated university of leeds college. this includes students who have completed the leeds international summer school or a study abroad programme at the university of leeds. register for an award leading to a postgraduate qualification (detailed in the eligible courses information on this page). be self-funding for at least part of the cost of your tuition fees. the alumni discount can be combined with other university of leeds scholarships and awards. eligible courses most of our postgraduate qualifications including the law llb conversion course are eligible for the alumni discount, except for the following: ba, bsc, masters, research degree or phd when studied as an intercalating part of a bachelor of medicine and surgery (mbchb) or bachelor of dentistry (bchd) jointly awarded degrees programmes that are part of professional training (not including postgraduate certificates, diplomas or masters degrees) integrated undergraduate masters degrees, such as meng, mbiol integrated phds pgce courses. terms and conditions students who have their fees paid in full by a sponsor (i.e. an employer, government, research council, charity or other third-party organisation) or the university of leeds are not eligible for the discount. the university will pay 10% of the self-funded part of your tuition fees (fees paid by yourself, a friend or family member, or a postgraduate loan from the uk government). the following courses are not eligible as qualifying previous qualifications: language centre pre-sessional courses. courses that are part of professional training or continued professional development (cpd) that are not postgraduate certificates, diplomas or masters qualifications. occasional study courses. english language foundation courses. the discount is applied automatically for each year of study and will take the form of a tuition fee discount, and no monies will be paid directly to you. this will reduce the amount payable to the university. the remainder of the tuition fee is then payable according to our tuition fee policy. the fee discount is not applicable during any year(s) abroad or year(s) in industry. the alumni discount will not require repaying if you leave partway through your studies. it will be assessed pro-rata, to coincide with the procedure for calculating outstanding tuition fees. you can receive the alumni discount twice, for example if you register for a masters degree followed by a research degree. the discount will not be applied during the overtime (writing-up) period for research degree students, for taught students who are re-sitting examinations, or for student visitors undertaking miscellaneous study. the university reviews the alumni discount annually and reserves the right to vary or withdraw this discount at its sole discretion. however, any changes will not be applied retrospectively. how to apply you do not need to complete an application form for the alumni discount. if you are eligible, it will be automatically applied to your record upon registration. disclaimer our scholarships directory provides information about scholarships available at the university of leeds. this directory is for information purposes only and does not constitute an offer of a scholarship. information about scholarships, including eligibility criteria, deadlines, and availability, may change from time to time. you should always refer to the full terms and conditions of any scholarship before applying. scholarship offers are made through a separate process. in the event that a scholarship offer is made in error, the university reserves the right to review and, where appropriate, withdraw or amend that offer prior to the student's acceptance. once an offer has been accepted, the university will act in accordance with the applicable scholarship terms and conditions.

pages.https://www.leeds.ac.uk/scholarship/7/sa: skip to main content university of leeds homepage search leeds.ac.uk search all leeds.ac.uk sanctuary scholarship we offer scholarships for forced migrants to the uk. the sanctuary scholarship is open to people who wish to study any undergraduate or masters degree. value full cost of tuition fees and £10000 a year towards study costs. fee status uk study level undergraduate, postgraduate, foundation final deadline this scholarship is closed for applications contact details email the sanctuary scholarships team at sanctuaryscholarships@leeds.ac.uk . country/region united kingdom eligibility degrees you can study you can apply for this scholarship if you have an offer or if you have applied for any of the following degrees, full-time or part-time: any 3 or 4 year undergraduate degree (including foundation degrees and degrees with an integrated masters). any masters degree which is not 100% online with the digital education service. exclusions you cannot apply for a sanctuary scholarship for: standalone foundation year courses postgraduate research and phd study. criteria you must: be a forced migrant to the united kingdom. this means you are a person displaced from your homeland or place of residence for political, economic, ethnic, environmental, or human rights pressures. you must have one of the residency statuses listed in 'eligible residency statuses' on this page . be unable to access mainstream funding, for example from student finance england or a local authority grant. have already applied to study at the university. you do not need to have an offer of a place yet. not have a degree from a uk university of the same level or higher than the course you want to study at leeds. be eligible to pay tuition fees at the uk rate. if you receive an offer to study that states you must pay tuition fees at the international rate, make sure you use the fee assessment process to confirm that this is correct. eligible residency statuses your residency status must be either: asylum seeker – currently seeking asylum within the uk, or refused asylum seeker where your application for refugee status has been denied and a fresh claim has already been submitted. limited or discretionary leave to remain. indefinite leave to remain if you have previously held one of the other statuses on this page since arriving in the uk. your status may also be one of the following, which are only eligible if you already have a degree of the same level you wish to study at leeds gained from a university outside of the uk, therefore making you ineligible for mainstream student funding: refugee status or the spouse or child of someone with refugee status. humanitarian protection status or the spouse or child of someone with humanitarian protection status. section 67 leave or the dependent child of someone with section 67 leave. calais leave. stateless person leave or the spouse or child of someone with stateless person leave. granted leave in the uk under the afghan relocations and assistance policy (arap) or the afghan citizens resettlement scheme (acrs). granted leave in the uk under the ukraine family scheme, the homes for ukraine sponsorship scheme or the ukraine extension scheme. we can only award the scholarship if your immigration status allows you to study for the duration of your course. if your immigration permission changes so that you are not allowed to study, we may have to cancel the scholarship. if you have decided not to receive student finance for faith reasons, this does not make you eligible for the sanctuary scholarship. for sharia-compliant funding opportunities, visit our page on financial support for muslim students . language requirements no specific language requirements are needed for the sanctuary scholarship. however, to obtain an offer to study on your programme, there will be english language requirements. to find out the english language requirements for your course, please contact your course's admissions team, which can be found on the course search page. if you are successful in obtaining a sanctuary scholarship, you will be assessed for suitability for a fully-funded place on a summer pre-sessional language course which can help you meet the language requirements for your course. how to apply scholarships are limited, and you must apply. if your application is successful, we will invite you to an interview. applications for the scholarship for 2026 entry are now closed. information about scholarships for 2027 entry will be released in early 2027. disclaimer our scholarships directory provides information about scholarships available at the university of leeds. this directory is for information purposes only and does not constitute an offer of a scholarship. information about scholarships, including eligibility criteria, deadlines, and availability, may change from time to time. you should always refer to the full terms and conditions of any scholarship before applying. scholarship offers are made through a separate process. in the event that a scholarship offer is made in error, the university reserves the right to review and, where appropriate, withdraw or amend that offer prior to the student's acceptance. once an offer has been accepted, the university will act in accordance with the applicable scholarship terms and conditions.

pages.https://www.scholarships.unsw.edu.au/wes: skip to main content westpac future leaders scholarship background the westpac future leaders scholarship supports australia's future leaders by providing an enriching postgraduate experience for talented individuals to study at one of australia's leading universities and participate in a bespoke, nine-month, leadership development program. about the scholarship "do you have the drive to make a difference?" whether your focus is asia, new technology or sustainable futures the westpac scholars trust is offering postgraduate study for talented individuals at australia's leading universities. scholars will be exceptional people, chosen for their potential to make a difference to australia's future in one of our four focus areas: sustainable futures asia-pacific leadership connected and stronger society innovation for impact the scholarships are valued at up to $120000 over 2-3 years and will be awarded annually for research or coursework studies at the graduate level. if you are commencing a phd or masters by coursework or masters by research in 2027, apply before thursday, 20 august 2026, 5:00pm (aest). an online information session will be held on 1pm aest, thursday, 23 july 2026. register here scholarship benefits up to $120000 over 2-3 years to cover the cost of study (e.g. course fees, living allowance, travel and conference attendance). enrolment in a nine-month leadership development program. opportunity to add a global context to your education, with tailored international experiences of up to six months. lifelong membership on the westpac 100 scholars network. attendance at the westpac scholars summit in march/april 2027 in sydney. what does it take to be a westpac future leaders scholar? key dates 24 june 2026 applications open 23 july 2026 westpac future leaders scholarship information session- click here to register your attendance. 20 august 2026 applications close (5:00pm, aest) 23-24 november 2026 national assessment centre in sydney mid-december 2026 notification of outcome how to apply? applications will open from 24 june 2026! for information on how to apply please visit the westpac scholars trust website . more information contact westpac scholars trust: westpacscholars@westpac.com.au hear from our students be prepared: the application process for the westpac future leaders scholarship has a few stages, each exploring a different facet of you as a person, from the way you approach various situations to your passions, motivations and aspirations. while the process spans a few months, it also provided an incredibly rewarding journey of introspection. sitting down and translating all these abstract concepts in my mind into a cohesive application allowed me to crystallise my values and what drives me as a person. practice: the national assessment centre and interview can sound incredibly intimidating—i felt the same way too! however, with good preparation and practice, the interview is such an invaluable opportunity to truly delve into what makes you unique. in addition to translating goals onto paper as part of the application, it was really empowering to articulate these values and goals to family, friends and anyone who would listen in preparation for the interview. each different audience had diverse perspectives and probing questions, which challenged me to think about my goals in unexpected ways. additionally, it was such a privilege to meet the inspiring leaders who comprise the selection panel and to learn from their invaluable insights. be authentic: the westpac future leaders scholarship interview is all about you as an individual. authentic leadership entails resilience and continuing to persevere despite setbacks. while it may appear intuitive to portray yourself as the 'perfect' person, you will gain so much more out of the interview process by acknowledging vulnerability and by exploring how moments of challenges have irrevocably shaped your identity. there are so many diverse scholarships on offer for postgraduate study, but the westpac future leaders scholarship stands out amongst them all. unlike other scholarships, the future leaders scholarship is focused not only on study, but on you as an individual and your personal development. it is all about leadership potential and vision, more so than finding the perfect leader, and being authentic is the greatest testament to this. elizabeth wong westpac scholar, 2022 future leader unsw my name is jaffly chen. i'm a medical doctor and a 2019 westpac future leaders scholar, and i'm passionate about rural and indigenous medicine. i want to help close the gap and transform our rural healthcare system - a bold ambition but one i am deeply committed to achieving. a year ago, when i came across the westpac future leaders scholarship, i really struggled with whether or not i should put myself forward for this. but i am so glad i did. here is a letter i have written to the person i was a year ago, perhaps where you find yourself right now, to share the impact that the scholarship has had on me over the last 12 months and how it has helped equip me with the tools i'm going to need to achieve my goals and make a real difference. if you're grappling with some career decisions, i hope this letter will help you to take the leap of faith, as i did, and apply for a scholarship that could change your life. dear (past) jaffly, congratulations, you've almost finished your first degree! yes, i know it's a very busy time right now - you're applying for jobs next year, thinking about what masters might be a good fit, and you've got that conference coming up next week! but just take a seat and hear me out okay buddy? what if i told the westpac future leaders scholarship could support you fully throughout your post-graduate studies, covering your tuition, living expenses, conferences, and international experiences – including going to mit and harvard to study healthcare innovation!? how incredible would it be to attend a bespoke leadership program as part of the scholarship - taught by some of the world's best leadership experts? you'll be challenged, much more than you thought possible, but don't panic. you'll grow, reflect, become empowered, and develop into a much better leader for it. never before have you come across a group of people so varied and interesting, and so unconditionally supportive of your dreams, ambitions, and passions. you'll come to realise this scholarship is about so much more than just the future leader scholars who are on this learning journey with you. the asian exchange scholars, young technologists, social change fellows and research fellows are all inspirational and supportive and you'll join the w100 network who are every bit as invested in helping you to succeed. you'll also realise that it's not about whether you match up, but how you can utilise your unique talents and strengths to help others succeed too. trust me. i promise you that joining the westpac family will be one of the best opportunities imaginable. you miss 100% of the shots you don't take. so take that shot because it's the first step to investing in yourself and creating a better tomorrow. it will be one of the best decisions you'll ever make. go rock some socks off! (present) jaffly ps – i'll be really mad if you don't apply. jaffly chen westpac scholar, 2019 future leader to be announced as one of the 2021 westpac future leaders scholars still catches me in disbelief and getting the call to let me know i was successful following of the panel interviews at the national assessment centre tops life's 'pinch me' moments. i initially heard about the scholarship through word of mouth and having my lab as a support system pushed and inspired me to apply. countless questions and subsequent hesitations were insurmountable but having had team members apply in previous years made it less intimidating. the thing that catalysed me into action and struck me most about the scholarship was the opportunity to become a part of an established and wonderful network of individuals known as the w100. to be able to expand my own individual network by gaining knowledge and insight from people of all different backgrounds was something that i wanted to tap into and if given the opportunity, to make the most out of. fast forward to stressful weeks of preparation, working on my application, video pitches and participating in a number of zoom interviews was a difficult process. despite this, the thing i found most challenging about the rounds was the inability to attend the final assessment centre in person, to meet and build rapport with other students and scholars in my cohort. to know that we will see each other this year during our residential leadership programs and the westpac scholars summit is reassuring. my advice to future applicants applying for this scholarship is to enjoy the ride. it is a rollercoaster full of highs and lows, but we must treat each trough and peak all the same. even though it was difficult, the application process taught me so much about myself. what i appreciated most was the fact westpac was not looking for the most exceptional student, freshly graduated with high distinctions and the highest of honours. they were interested in learning about me, and i had the opportunity to showcase myself. so, when the spotlight appears, have your moment, and enjoy it. even though everything is still new and fresh, it has been wonderful experience so far, connecting with the w100 network and being a part of this community. monica phimmachanh westpac scholar, 2021 future leader there are a number of important questions to ask when deciding to undertake postgraduate studies. first, there's the big one – what do i want to study and why? more than anything this decision must be driven by passion. what makes you tick, what are you curious about, how do you want to make the world a better place? after working for a few years on policy problems, my answer to this emerged. i found a deep passion of cities and wanted to understand how they could be built, revitalised and managed to create more inclusive and sustainable places to live. the second big question is of course where should i study? answering this was pretty easy for me. i was drawn to unsw for its world renowned built environment faculty, strong industry links, and the opportunity to explore the ever-dynamic sydney as a live-in laboratory urban planning. and then there are a myriad of questions relating to how. how will this fit in with my life and career? how will i support myself throughout the process? and how can i get the most out of my postgraduate experience? my answers to these questions came in the form of a once in a life time scholarship – the westpac future leaders scholarship. the westpac future leader scholarship is a comprehensive scholarship that supports you in studies and personal development. on top of financial support covering fees, living costs, equipment, conferences, and adding an overseas component to your studies, future leaders scholars also participate in a bespoke leadership development program, and join a community of other talented and driven westpac scholars as part of the westpac 100 scholars network. each year 17 scholarships valuing up to $120000 each are awarded across australia. recipients are chosen based on their past experiences and vision to shape australia. receiving this scholarship has completely transformed my postgraduate experience. in a field as broad as urban planning, the westpac scholarship has afforded me the flexibility to explore different parts of the planning profession. this has included attending conferences in australia and overseas, where i have learnt from leading voices in my field and been exposed to new ideas. i've also been able to initiate projects with peers, and change jobs to find work that aligned with my interests. my fellow westpac scholars have been an important part of my studies. while we come from a variety of disciplines – neuroscience, law, agriculture, medicine, and engineering to name a few – we're united in our desire to excel in our fields and make an impact in the world around us. our catch-up coffees and interstate reunions have been a source of support and motivation, and a key point of reflection – to zoom out from our particular area of study and to see a bigger picture. choosing to apply for this scholarship two years ago is one of the best decisions i made. if you're planning to undertake postgraduate study, have a passion for your field and a vision to contribute to a better australia, you should apply today. elise wood westpac future leaders scholar previous next haven't found what you're looking for? contact us talk to a member of our scholarships team faqs most prizes are awarded annually for academic achievement in particular units or programs of study. applications are not required as students are nominated by the relevant faculty according to mid-year and final-year academic results. for example, there are approximately 600 prizes awarded annually (at a value of $1000 each) as part of the university of sydney academic merit prize. these awards were established in 2007 to recognise exemplary undergraduate students. the awards aim to both acknowledge and promote student academic excellence. if you win a university of sydney academic merit prize you will receive $1000 and your achievement will be recorded on your transcript. literary prizes do require an application as well as the submission of written work. what happens if i win a prize? prize winners are notified via email. current students will be contacted at their university email address. to receive payment you must ensure your bank details are up-to-date in the myfinance tab in sydney student . if your most recent bank details are correct in sydney student, you do not need to do anything further. if you need to update your bank details and cannot log into sydney student, please complete the supplier details request form (pdf, 62kb) and email it to scholarships.office@sydney.edu.au . how to fill out the supplier details request form tick add new supplier . enter your name in 'supplier name'. do not tick 'abn' or 'no abn '. complete all of the 'supplier contact details' and 'bank details' sections. include your name and sign at the bottom of the form. provide a copy of a bank statement or bank letter verifying your bank account details. prizes and awards faculty prizes h2 learn more about faculty prizes and awards established to recognise students for their outstanding academic achievement in various units or programs of study. faculty prizes learn more about faculty prizes and awards established to recognise students for their outstanding academic achievement in various units or programs of study. literary prizes h2 learn more about literary prizes that have been established to recognise and celebrate our students' achievements in literature. literary prizes learn more about literary prizes that have been established to recognise and celebrate our students' achievements in literature. university-wide prizes h2 learn more about university wide prizes that have been established to recognise our students for their overall outstanding academic achievement. university-wide prizes learn more about university wide prizes that have been established to recognise our students for their overall outstanding academic achievement.

visiting fellowships university of southampton malaysia partnerships and initiatives online master's degrees postgraduate funding options there are many ways to help fund your postgraduate studies at southampton. your options will depend on what course you're studying and where you're from. ways to fund your postgraduate studies loans and grants check if you can apply for a loan or grant from the uk government to help fund your postgraduate studies. scholarships explore our full range of scholarships to see what funding you're eligible for. funding from research councils find out if you can apply for tuition fee funding or a maintenance grant through a uk research council. available to uk and eu students only. self funded student support fund if you experience unexpected financial difficulties like the loss of your job during your studies, you may be eligible for a single discretionary payment to help. phd funding funded phd studentships find a funded phd studentship on our university recruitment pages. funded doctoral training programmes funded doctoral training programmes offer fully funded studentships for up to 4 years. presidential scholarships postgraduate research scholarships, or "presidential scholarships", fund part or all of your tuition fees, a stipend and a support grant for up to 3.5 years. engineering doctorate our 4 year engineering doctorate (engd) runs in collaboration with an industry sponsor. it combines advanced technical and management training with phd level research. british federation of women graduates charities administered by the british federation of women graduates sometimes make awards women graduates undertaking doctoral research. knowledge transfer partnerships study for your master's or phd while working with a company in your industry, and managing a strategic project. help and advice additional support our student support services can help you with anything from wellbeing to study skills. cost of living understanding the costs of student living in southampton can help you make informed choices about your finances and support you may need. get in touch you can contact the student hub or the students' union if you have any questions about fees or funding. student hub +44 (0)23 8059 9599 stufunds@southampton.ac.uk building 37, highfield campus, university road, southampton, so17 1bj students' union for a phd or research degree how to make a phd enquiry support while studying your phd or research degree understanding how your research degree will be funded is a key step in the application process. depending on the type of project you want to apply for, there are different routes to fund your fees. we offer: fully funded projects that cover the costs of your tuition fees and an allowance (stipend) projects that fund your tuition fees only opportunities to explore your own research proposal where you'll need to source your own funding it's important to know where your funding will come from before applying for a project. funded projects for projects advertised as 'fully funded' or 'competition funded', your university fees will be paid and you will not need to apply for additional funding. competition funded projects will go ahead if the funding is awarded by the funding body. you can talk with the main supervisor to find out more. funding may also be available within the relevant school or faculty. learn more in the fees and funding section of your chosen phd topic areas . see our current research degree projects fees paid plus a living allowance a funded project will cover your tuition fees. some projects come with an additional sum of money to cover things like accommodation, travel and maintenance expenses. this is called a stipend and is tax free. fees paid with no living allowance some project funding will only cover your university fees. you will need to cover your living expenses yourself. if you need help to cover your living costs, uk students can apply for a doctoral loan through student finance england. international students can check if they are eligible to receive a scholarship or bursary . fees for 2026/27 you can find all our current fees for 2026/27 on our fees page . projects advertised with no funding yet some advertised projects do not have funding secured yet. the main supervisor will usually source funding once they have found a suitable phd candidate. contact the main supervisor to find out about the specific funding options if there's a project you're interested in. funded doctoral training programmes our doctoral training programmes are sponsored by one of the ukri research councils and partners across government, industry, the nhs and charities. these types of programmes include: doctoral focal awards doctoral landscape awards doctoral training partnerships centres for doctoral training you can also check the details in the advertised project or specific doctoral training programme for how to apply. funding your own project you should tell your supervisor if you plan to self-fund your research project. you'll need to say how you intend to pay your fees when you apply. you could consider: university scholarships a postgraduate doctoral loan external funding bodies (charities, government and the private sector) combining different funding sources take out a doctoral loan you can apply for a government loan to cover your fees. doctoral loans are not means tested and you can decide how much you want to borrow. find out about doctoral loans on gov.uk apply for funding from a charity you may be able to win funding from 1 or more organisations to help fund your phd or research degree. learn about charity funding on findaphd get advice on funding your phd you can speak to the supervisor you wish you work with or contact the doctoral college by email: doctoral-college@soton.ac.uk support and money while studying get advice on general support and how to manage your money external funding opportunities fee status the university of southampton charges 2 levels of tuition fee: a lower 'uk' (or 'home) fee a higher 'international' (or 'overseas') fee the amount you pay will depend on which you meet the criteria for. this is your university 'fee status'. your fee status is based on the criteria for who should be charged home fees in england, as set out by the government in the education (fees and awards) (england) regulations 2007 as amended. we make our assessments in line with these regulations. for further information about the criteria please visit the uk council for international student affairs (ukcisa) . assessing your fee status we assess your fee status when you apply and will let you know your fee status and how much you'll pay in your offer letter. sometimes we might need more information to help us make the right decision. if so we'll ask you to complete our fee status questionnaire. if you believe that the fee status you have been assigned does not fit your circumstances, please contact us to discuss this matter. adjusting your fee status after your course has started there are some circumstances where you may become eligible for home fees after you have started your course. we recommend that you check whether you meet the requirements for any of the 'home' fee categories , and contact us if you think you need to change your fee status to 'home' fees in time for the next year of your course. uk council for international student affairs ukcisa provides advice and information to international students studying in the uk and to staff who work with them. information and advice to students is free. for more information, please visit ukcisa. contact us if you have any questions about your fee status once you have applied to us, please contact the admissions team. admissions 00 +44 (0)23 8059 4732 feesclassification@southampton.ac.uk useful links ukcisa study view all courses taught postgraduate study malaysia partnerships and initiatives online master's degrees understanding international scholarships international scholarships can help support the cost of studying at university in the uk. these awards are available to eligible international students and may contribute towards tuition fees, living expenses or other study-related costs. a scholarship is not a loan and does not have a repayment plan. this year marks 75 years since the university of southampton was granted its royal charter. to celebrate we're offering a new group of scholarships called the 75th anniversary excellence scholarships. there are a number of these awards available depending on your subject and country of permanent residence. you can find our awards through our scholarships search tool. find a scholarship search our scholarships by country, course or subject to find funding opportunities you're eligible for. types of international scholarships some of our scholarships are linked to specific courses or subjects, while others are more general. you should always read the details of the scholarship you're interested in as the eligibility criteria and application processes vary. scholarships may be funded solely by the university of southampton or in partnership with government schemes, charities or external organisations. we separate our scholarships into 3 categories: awarded automatically, needs application, and external scholarships. awarded automatically these awards may be given based on academic achievement or your country of permanent residence. additional eligibility criteria for these scholarships vary so you must read the details of your chosen scholarship carefully. if you meet the criteria for one of these scholarships when you apply to your chosen course, we'll let you know by email. these scholarships are awarded on a first come first served basis. needs application these are sometimes referred to as competitive scholarships. if a scholarship requires an application it will be clearly marked on it's page. to be awarded, you'll need to have an existing offer for your chosen course and meet additional eligibility criteria. your application may ask for evidence of academic achievement, a portfolio or other evidence appropriate to the eligibility criteria. because this is a competitive process, not all applications will be successful. if your application is successful, you'll get an email explaining how you'll receive it. external scholarships these scholarships are awarded in partnership between the university of southampton and external organisations and may require an application through a separate website. you may also be eligible for funding in your home country to help cover the costs of studying at a uk university. these are not listed in our search tool and we have no responsibility for their allocation. bursaries while scholarships are awarded for academic achievement or other similar criteria, and essentially give you a discount on your tuition fees, a bursary is usually means-tested and intended to support living costs for those experiencing financial difficulty. you may see some in our scholarship search tool results. like scholarships, they do not need to be repaid, but they will come with different terms and conditions. you cannot receive both a scholarship and a bursary at the same time. how to apply for an international scholarship before you apply for a scholarship you must check the individual eligibility requirements and application process, but as a general rule you will need to: have already applied to study your chosen course be paying an overseas tuition fee be funding your studies yourself, rather than being sponsored by an external organisation there may be some exceptions, so read the specific scholarship information carefully. check what fees you'll pay application deadlines if your scholarship requires an application, make sure to note the deadline and submit your application in time. grade equivalencies to get a scholarship you must meet the requirements of your chosen course. this will include qualifications equivalent to specific grades at a-level. what your grades equate to will depend on where you were awarded your qualification. check your country's grade equivalencies terms and conditions all of the scholarships we fund are subject to terms and conditions in addition to their individual requirements. external scholarships may be subject to their own at the discretion of the provider. help and advice have a question about international scholarships? our friendly scholarships team can support and guide you. international-scholarships@soton.ac.uk we're open monday to friday 9am to 5pm, uk time useful links find a course scholarship students from forced migration backgrounds, with no access to uk financial support on this page overview scholarship applications for 2026-27 are now closed. this information is for guidance only. 4 sanctuary scholarships are available for students from forced migration backgrounds: 1 for undergraduate, 3 for postgraduate taught courses. what you get tuition fee cover for all years of study a bursary for each year of study to help with living costs support with university accommodation a welcome pack deadline closed eligibility to get this scholarship you must: have an offer to study at the university of southampton be an asylum seeker or included as a dependent (e.g. a child or spouse of the applicant) awaiting a decision on your asylum claim or be in the appeals process have received a decision on your asylum claim but been given a new visa status that does not allow access to uk government financial support like tuition fee or maintenance loans or give you a uk (or 'home') fee status. check your fee status if you're not sure if you can apply or not, or what other support you may be able to apply for, contact our sanctuary officer, claire giles. spouses or civil partners must have been the spouse or civil partner on the date on which the asylum application to the uk government was made. children and step-children must have been aged under 18 on the date on which the asylum application to the uk government was made. all applications will be considered, but if you are in any of these neighbouring areas your application will be given priority: dorset hampshire isle of wight wiltshire sussex west surrey immigration statuses we accept if you have been given one of these status', you can apply for this scholarship. asylum seekers limited leave to remain (llr) discretionary leave to remain (dlr) unaccompanied asylum-seeking child (uasc) if you are an asylum seeker you should provide your application registration card (arc) card as evidence. if you have llr, dlr or uasc status, you should provide your evisa share code or other documentation as evidence. in some circumstances you might be eligible for student finance and therefore not eligible for the sanctuary scholarship. immigration statuses we do not accept if you have one of these status' you cannot apply for this scholarship. you might however be eligible for student finance. for more information on what funding support you can apply for, check our fees and funding pages . calais leave stateless leave 67 leave humanitarian protection afghan relocations and assistance policy (arap) afghan citizens resettlement scheme (acrs) indefinite leave to remain (ilr) how to apply scholarship applications for 2026-27 are now closed. this information is for guidance only. apply to study an undergraduate or postgraduate programme find an undergraduate programme and apply through ucas or find a postgraduate taught programme and apply complete the sanctuary scholarship application form complete an application form and submit the following supporting evidence: your admissions letter evidence for your immigration claim or status a reference if you are unable to access the form or need a different format, please contact the sanctuary team. how we award there are 9 stages in the shortlisting process. the sanctuary officer will process the forms and may contact applicants should further information be required. the panel meet to go through completed applications after the submission deadlines for undergraduates and postgraduate. the panel selects the applicants they wish to offer the scholarship to. the sanctuary officer contacts successful applicants to offer them a conditional scholarship offer. this condition is based on being able to successfully enrol onto one of our university programmes and completing a right to study check. you then accept or decline the scholarship offer. if you decline, the panel will go back to the unsuccessful applicants to ask if they are still interested and eligible. in august you must confirm if you have met the requirements of your programme after results day. you must confirm whether accommodation is needed with the sanctuary officer and apply if needed. once confirmed and you have applied for accommodation you must complete a right to study check. the university will check your eligibility again in early september. do not move to southampton until you have had confirmation. if your application is successful, you will receive a confirmation email and award letter. help and advice university of sanctuary learn more about our status as a university of sanctuary and additional support with forced migration. help and advice if you have any questions or have specific accommodation requirements, get in touch with our sanctuary coordinator, claire giles. we're happy to help. claire giles sanctuary@soton.ac.uk useful links refugee education uk displaced students support sustainable development in their home country. key information funding type fully funded total value full tuition fees, a living allowance, travel costs and allowances application deadline closed eligibility study a full-time taught master's programme in development-focused subjects on this page overview commonwealth scholarships support talented students from low and middle income commonwealth countries to study in the uk. funded by uk foreign, commonwealth and development office (fcdo), they help develop future leaders and professionals who can contribute to sustainable development in their home countries. commonwealth scholarships particularly support candidates from disadvantaged backgrounds who may not otherwise be able to access uk postgraduate study. what you get tuition fees a monthly living allowance return travel costs an allowance package deadline tuesday 20 october 2026, 4pm uk time eligibility to get this scholarship you must: be a british protected person , a citizen of an eligible country, or a refugee living in an eligible country be permanently resident in one of the eligible countries be available to start your academic studies by the start of the uk academic year in september have a 2:1 honours degree, or a 2:2 degree and a relevant postgraduate qualification be unable to afford to study in the uk without this scholarship provide all supporting documentation in the required format you must also study a programme relating to one of the following themes: science and technology for development strengthening health systems and capacity promoting global prosperity strengthening global peace, security and governance strengthening resilience and response to crises access, inclusion and opportunity the commonwealth scholarship commission provides more information on this scholarship . the commission will normally only fund your first uk master's degree. you'll need to provide justification if you're applying for a second uk master's degree. show eligible countries bangladesh belize botswana dominica eswatini fiji gabon gambia ghana grenada guyana india jamaica kenya kiribati lesotho malawi malaysia maldives mauritius montserrat mozambique namibia nauru nigeria pakistan papua new guinea rwanda saint helena, ascension and tristan da cunha saint lucia saint vincent and the grenadines samoa sierra leone solomon islands south africa sri lanka tanzania togo tonga tuvalu uganda vanuatu zambia how to apply apply to study an eligible postgraduate programme you must indicate on your application form that you wish to be considered for commonwealth scholarship funding. find a postgraduate taught programme and apply apply for the scholarship apply through your local national nominating agency or non-governmental working towards my career aspirations. the support monash has given me has extended not just financially but it has also increased my own confidence to know that i have the support of others around me. being able to study in melbourne is an opportunity that i will never take for granted. am i eligible? you must be one of the following: an australian citizen a new zealand citizen australian permanent resident australian humanitarian visa holder you must meet the following criteria: current australian year 12 or international baccalaureate student. completed year 12 in previous year and has not undertaken any other tertiary study. benefits $8000 per annum (48 credit points of study) up to a maximum of four years. (for scholarships awarded from 2024). number offered unlimited – offered to all eligible students with an atar of 99.95. ten scholarships are available to the highest-achieving students who are indigenous australians **. **to be eligible you must provide a confirmation of aboriginal and/or torres strait islander heritage certificate or a certified statutory declaration form to the william cooper institute. this can be emailed to wci-ss@monash.edu. if you have any queries please contact the william cooper institute on 9902 4972. selection criteria for non-indigenous australians, awarded to all eligible students who achieve an atar of 99.95+ or equivalent for indigenous australians, awarded to the top ten eligible students who achieve an atar of 85.00+ or equivalent to retain this scholarship: you must maintain a minimum weighted average mark of 70 each semester for indigenous australians, you must maintain a minimum weighted average mark of 60 each semester how to apply no application is required all eligible students who list monash university as a vtac course preference will be automatically assessed this scholarship can be deferred every scholarship may have a different application process – or none at all. read the application details carefully and submit your application by the deadline. for more details, visit our scholarships application page . we use cookies to improve your experience, but you can choose which ones we use, and opt-out at any time. you can find more information in our website terms and conditions accept all cookie settings

ambition to change your future through undergraduate study at monash university, you may be eligible for the monash humanitarian scholarship. you will receive 100% international student funding for the monash undergraduate degree of your choice plus a yearly allowance of $6000. monash has increased the number of these scholarships available thanks to the generous donations from alumni and supporters of the university through the achieving potential fund. applications see below total scholarship value full course fees plus up to $30000 allowance number offered up to 34 see details niti manish kumar kakkad monash international merit scholarship monash university has ignited my passion for becoming a pharmaceutical scientist. engaging in cutting-edge research and collaborating with industry professionals has been both exciting and rewarding. this scholarship support has allowed me to focus on my academic and professional goals, further solidifying my commitment to advancing pharmaceutical science. am i eligible? you must be one of the following: an international student you must meet the following criteria: a person who is in australia currently on one of the below visas (and who has the relevant study rights in their visa conditions): temporary humanitarian stay visa (subclass 449) temporary protection visa (subclass 785) temporary humanitarian concern visa (subclass 786) safe haven enterprise visa (subclass 790) bridging visa a (subclass 010) or bridging visa e (subclass 050 and 051) (inactive visas included) or other appropriate bridging visa type and have applied for a permanent protection visa a commencing or continuing international student enrolled or intending to enrol in: an undergraduate degree at a monash university campus in australia, or a monash university foundation year or monash university diploma through monash college* have achieved a minimum atar of 70.00, or for current students a minimum weighted average mark (wam) of 60, or equivalent academic achievement. * monash college - should you successfully complete the monash college diploma and are eligible and offered a place in a monash university undergraduate degree you are eligible to continue receiving this scholarship. please note, your undergraduate degree must immediately proceed the completion of your diploma. benefits full international student course fees paid for the duration of the undergraduate degree. an allowance of $6000 per year (48 credit points of study) until the minimum credit points for your undergraduate degree are completed. number offered up to 34 note: number offered may be restricted based on availability within course faculty or discipline selection criteria awarded based on academic achievement. to retain this scholarship: you must maintain a pass average (50% or above) each semester. if your residency changes after your first semester of study, you can continue to receive the scholarship. however you will not be eligible to continue to receive tuition payments if you are changed to a commonwealth supported place and are eligible to defer your fees, but you may continue to receive the allowance. you may be asked to provide an annual progress report to donors, giving you an opportunity to share your experiences and benefits. how to apply non-vtac applicants and current students if you are a current monash student or applying directly to monash for your course, or a school leaver on bridging visa b,c or d you will need to complete a separate application form to be considered. applications opening on monday 3 august 2026, applications closing on sunday 6 december 2026. for semester 2 offers, you must receive a undergraduate course offer, or be enrolled in an undergraduate course, with monash university by tuesday, 12 january 2027 to be considered. this scholarship is not available for postgraduate students. vtac applicants vtac applicants will be automatically considered for this scholarship if you apply for the vtac equity scheme (seas) between monday 3 august (9am) and friday 9 october (5pm) and meet the scholarship eligibility requirements. you must have a monash course listed as at least one of your course preferences in vtac to be considered. every scholarship may have a different application process. read the application details carefully and submit your application by the deadline. total scholarship value up to $3000 number offered 430 see details alyna mithani monash kickstart scholarship moving to a new country with my family was stressful, and it was a difficult decision to make. coming from a single-income family, most of our stress stemmed from the financial situation we were put in. i am grateful that the scholarship has given me an advantage and has helped me deal with the financial stress of my studies. this scholarship has driven me to work hard and strive for the best. it's easy to let things become stressful; however, i believe great things can be achieved with hard work and the proper support. am i eligible? you must be one of the following: an australian citizen a new zealand citizen australian permanent resident australian humanitarian visa holder you must meet the following criteria: have experienced difficult family and life circumstances or living with a disability or medical condition that has affected your ability to engage with study. malaysia partnerships and initiatives online master's degrees spärck ai scholarship there are 11 scholarships available covering full tuition fees and a yearly living allowance of £20780 inline with ukri stipend rates . the spärck ai scholarships are open to uk and international students applying to study an eligible postgraduate course. you'll also get: national ai-related networking opportunities with leading academics, government contacts and industry leaders access to priority work placements with leading uk artificial intelligence companies and government institutions deadline to apply: applications for the 2026 scholarship are now closed. the information on this page is for reference only. we will update this page with details for 2027 entry in autumn 2026. eligibility to be eligible for this scholarship you must: apply and receive an offer to study an eligible university of southampton course be able to start your studies in the uk when the academic year starts in september 2026 not receive any external sponsorship covering 100% of tuition fees not receive any other form of uk government funding be able to attend the national in person spärck ai launch event in manchester on the 9th and 10th september 2026, (reasonable costs for travel expenses will be provided) eligible courses msc machine learning msc artificial intelligence msc robotics and autonomous systems msc data and decision analytics msc digital chemistry scholarship application guidelines please make sure you read the following documents before starting your application: 8.03 kb application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text spärck ai scholarship scheme summary 14.18 kb application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text spärck ai scholarship application guidelines how to apply to apply for this scholarship: apply and receive an offer to study an eligible university of southampton course by completing our programme application form, which you can find on our course pages familiarise yourself with the scholarship application guidelines and summary documents provided on this page complete and submit the online scholarship application form by 15 april 2026, 11.59pm (uk time) apply now we will contact you by the end of june 2026 to confirm the outcome of your scholarship application. if your application is successful you'll receive confirmation in an email with an attached letter. we cannot accept late applications. how we award scholarships there are 6 stages to the award process: we check you meet the eligibility criteria your academic record and qualifications on your postgraduate application form are scored your personal statement and essay in your scholarship application form is assessed against the core attributes required for this award we consider the reference you provided to support your application shortlisted applicants will then be invited to an interview a selection panel will decide on who gets the scholarships the selection panel may also consider balancing scholarship awards across the eligible courses available. consideration will also be given to those coming from underrepresented and minoritised groups. this is a competitive process and not all applications will be successful. the decision of the scholarship panel is final. help and advice have a question about this scholarship? our friendly scholarships team can support open, a link to the application form will be available on this page. apply to study a faculty of arts and humanities programme find a postgraduate taught programme and apply complete the scholarship application form as part of your application, you will need to submit a supporting statement of 250 words or fewer explaining: why you have selected your chosen course how your chosen course relates to your previous academic or professional experience how your chosen course relates to your future academic or professional goals how your goals will contribute towards creating a more sustainable and inclusive world late applications cannot be accepted. how we award there are 5 stages in the shortlisting process. we check that you meet the eligibility criteria and score and rank the academic qualifications listed on your postgraduate application form. we shortlist candidates to recognise global talent and support a diverse university community, including applicants from least developed, low-income and lower middle-income countries. we score and rank the supporting statement included in your application. we shortlist candidates from across the school of humanities and winchester school of art to recognise academic excellence across all subject areas. a panel chaired by the dean of faculty of arts and humanities, or their nominated representative, decides who receives the scholarships. this is a competitive process, and not all applications will be successful. the scholarship panel's decision is final. we do not provide feedback on applications or decisions. if your application is successful, you will receive a confirmation email and award letter. if you're awarded more than one university of southampton scholarship, you'll automatically receive the highest-value award. help and advice help and advice have a question about this scholarship? our friendly scholarships team can support and guide you. international-scholarships@soton.ac.uk we're open monday to zambia zimbabwe åland islands how to apply scholarship applications open in october 2026. once applications open, a link to the application form will be available on this page. apply to study a faculty of engineering and physical sciences programme find your programme and apply complete the scholarship application form as part of your scholarship application you will be required to submit a supporting statement of up to 250 words explaining : why you have selected your chosen course how your chosen course relates to your previous academic or professional experience how your chosen course relates to your future academic or professional goals how your goals will contribute towards creating a more sustainable and inclusive world late applications cannot be accepted. how we award there are 5 stages in the shortlisting process. we check that you meet the eligibility criteria and score and rank the academic qualifications listed on your application form. we shortlist candidates to recognise global talent and support a diverse university community, including applicants from least developed, low-income and lower middle-income countries. we score and rank the supporting statement included in your application. we shortlist candidates from across the faculty of engineering and physical sciences to recognise academic excellence across all subject areas. a panel chaired by the dean of faculty of engineering and physical sciences, or their nominated representative, decides who receives the scholarships. this is a competitive process, and not all applications will be successful. the scholarship panel's decision is final. we do not provide feedback on applications or decisions. if your application is successful, you will receive a confirmation email and award letter. if you're awarded more than one university of southampton scholarship, you'll automatically receive the highest-value award. help and advice help and advice have a question about this university in melbourne, australia. this scholarship supports outstanding students from african countries to pursue their academic goals at rmit university in melbourne, australia. scholarships / scholarships for commencing international students / this scholarship supports outstanding students from african countries to pursue their academic goals at rmit university in melbourne, australia. value and duration the value of the scholarship is a 20% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the eligible program(s)* as outlined in your offer letter. eligibility in order to qualify for this scholarship you must: be a citizen of countries in africa be an international student holding a valid student visa or plan to apply for a student visa prior to the program commencement achieve australian equivalent grade gpa of 2.5 or 70% average or atar 75 in your qualifying qualification at the time of application hold a full or conditional offer letter commencing in 2026 or later in vocational education, associate degree*, bachelor's degree*, graduate certificate, graduate diploma or masters by coursework program not be an existing rmit university student (existing elicos or foundation studies may qualify and will be notified after foundation studies completion). * exclusions apply to the following programs: ad023 associate degree in aviation (professional pilots) bp345 bachelor of aviation (pilot training) how to apply select an eligible program submit an application to study at rmit no scholarship application is required terms and conditions the scholarship is made available effective from 3 december 2025. the scholarship is only applicable to tuition fees. scholarship selection is based on academic merit. the scholarship will be revoked if you no longer hold a student visa. the scholarship is only applicable to the eligible program(s) and duration on your initial offer letter. successful applicants will be notified. if you do not receive an outcome, your application has not been successful. successful applicants may be invited to participate and get involved in the rmit melbourne open day. the scholarship will be revoked if you are granted any rmit or australian funded scholarships covering tuition fees. applicants with foundation studies packaged offer starting from february 2026 may be eligible. a notification will be sent once your foundation studies final results are available. applicants should not be in receipt of any other rmit funded scholarship or australia awards scholarship covering tuition fees. it's important to note that this scholarship has limited availability and will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. to secure your scholarship you must accept your offer and make a deposit payment within 14 days from the date of offer letter. students who are already granted the academic merit scholarship are allowed to change program in future semester, the scholarship will continue apply to a new program as long as a new program is not under the exclusion list above. for full terms and conditions, please view the international scholarships terms and conditions document . contact ask us a question about scholarships or study options for international students at rmit university. contact study@rmit explore more meet rmit staff in your country browse events by country ready to apply? learn about entry pages.https://www.ntu.edu.sg/admissions/gradua: privacy notice this site uses cookies to offer you a better browsing experience. by continuing, you are agreeing to the use of cookies on your device as described in our privacy policy . close toggle notification toggle search toggle menu search nanyang president's graduate scholarship the nanyang president's graduate scholarship (npgs) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme designed to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying for a full time phd at ntu. the premier scholarship granted by ntu's president, recognizing phd students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities. eligibility all nationalities are eligible for the scholarship. an honours (highest distinction) or equivalent at bachelor's level. candidates who have not yet completed their undergraduate degree must provide official documentation from their university confirming they are on track to graduate with an honours (highest distinction) degree or equivalent. coverage and award terms there is no bond attached to the scholarship. the award is tenable for one year in the first instance and is renewable subject to good progress. the maximum period of the scholarship is 4 years for phd candidates, as determined by school as well as availability of research funding in each case. ​ citizenship ​singapore citizen 1 ​singapore permanent resident ​international student 2 revised monthly stipend for students with effect from january 2026. the stipend remains the same for existing students receiving higher stipend rates. ​ monthly stipend s$5300 s$4800 s$4300 other allowances overseas conference allowance up to s$5000* per financial year (april previous year to march current year) book allowance annual grant of s$500 ​ ​ it allowance one time allowance of s$1500​ ​ ​ thesis allowance one time allowance of s$600 it will be disbursed during the final year scholarship renewal. ​ ​ 1 central provident fund (cpf) contributions shall be provided at a rate pegged to the prevailing employer's contribution rate set by cpf, on top of the monthly stipend received. 2 international students must perform teaching/ laboratory supervision duties to fulfil the requirements of the graduate assistantship programme (gap) . singaporeans and singapore permanent residents may perform gap at the discretion of the schools. *revised overseas conference allowance with effect from april 2026 this award also covers the annual tuition fee. priority will be given for campus accommodation. scholarship coverage and award terms are subject to change. the university reserves the right to vary the amount of the award stipend at any time. new students to take note: please update your singapore bank account details in student intranet (gslink) before 15th of the semester commencement month (january or august) to avoid delays in stipend payment. the one-time it allowance will be disbursed automatically after the bank details have been updated. [back to top] application procedure academic year 2027-2028 the application period for academic year 2027–2028 will be from 1 november 2026 to 31 december 2026. for the national institute of education (nie), the application period will be from 2 november 2026 to 30 december 2026. interested applicants may submit their applications through the graduate programmes application exercise | national institute of education (nie) | ntu singapore during the application period. this scholarship is by nomination only. shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview and be evaluated by the university as part of the selection process. supporting documents to be uploaded in the online application: identification documents education qualifications (in both original language and official translation in english) research proposal two referee reports other supporting documents: resume research publications test scores (i.e. ielts/toefl/gre/gmate/gate), where applicable apply here notification of award successful candidates will be informed on the outcome of their application together with the offer of admissions via email. they are required to observe the terms and conditions for the award of the scholarship.

be available on this page. apply to study a faculty of environmental and life sciences programme find your programme and apply complete the scholarship application form as part of your scholarship application you will be required to submit a supporting statement of up to 250 words explaining : why you have selected your chosen course how your chosen course relates to your previous academic or professional experience how your chosen course relates to your future academic or professional goals how your goals will contribute towards creating a more sustainable and inclusive world we cannot accept late applications. how we award there are 6 stages in the shortlisting process. we check that you meet the eligibility criteria and score and rank the academic qualifications listed on your application form. we shortlist candidates to recognise global talent and support a diverse university community, including applicants from least developed, low-income and lower middle-income countries. we score and rank the supporting statement included in your application. we shortlist candidates from across the faculty of environmental and life sciences to recognise academic excellence across all subject areas. shortlisted candidates will be invited to an on-line scholarship interview. a panel chaired by the dean of faculty of environmental and life sciences, or their nominated representative, decides who receives the scholarships. this is a competitive process, and not all applications will be successful. the scholarship panel's decision is final. we do not provide feedback on applications or decisions. if your application is successful, you will receive a confirmation email and award letter. if you're awarded more than one university of southampton scholarship, you'll automatically receive the highest-value award. help and advice help and advice have a question about this scholarship? our friendly scholarships team can support and guide you. described in our privacy policy . close toggle notification toggle search toggle menu search provost graduate award the provost graduate award (pga) is a distinguished award presented by the ntu provost to phd students demonstrating outstanding academic achievements and research potential in their field of study. eligibility all nationalities are eligible for the scholarship. an honours (highest distinction) or equivalent at bachelor's level. candidates who have not yet completed their undergraduate degree must provide official documentation from their university confirming they are on track to graduate with an honours (highest distinction) degree or equivalent. coverage and award terms there is no bond attached to the scholarship. the award is tenable for one year in the first instance and is renewable subject to good progress. the maximum period of the award covers 4 years of the phd candidature. ​ citizenship ​singapore citizen 1 ​singapore permanent resident ​international student 2 revised monthly stipend for students with effect from january 2026. the stipend remains the same for existing students receiving higher stipend rates. ​ monthly stipend s$5300 s$4800 s$4300 *overseas conference allowance up to s$3000 per financial year (april previous year to march current year) 1 central provident fund (cpf) contributions shall be provided at a rate pegged to the prevailing employer's contribution rate set by cpf, on top of the monthly stipend received. 2 international students must perform teaching/ laboratory supervision duties to fulfil the requirements of the graduate assistantship programme (gap) . singaporeans and singapore permanent residents may perform gap at the discretion of the schools. this award also covers the annual tuition fee. scholarship coverage and award terms are subject to change. the university reserves the right to vary the amount of the award stipend at any time. *overseas conference allowance with effect from april 2026 new students to take note: please update your singapore bank account details in student intranet (gslink) before 15th of the semester commencement month (january or august) to avoid delays in stipend payment. [back to top] application procedure academic year 2026-2027 this award is by nomination only. shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview and be evaluated by the university as part of the selection process. supporting documents to be uploaded in the online application: identification documents education qualifications (in both original language and official translation in english) research proposal two referee reports other supporting documents: resume research publications test scores (i.e. ielts/toefl/gre/gmate/gate), where applicable apply here
